Handling objections is responding to customer concerns. Common objections: price ('too expensive'), timing ('not now'), product ('not a fit'), competition ('using competitor'). LAER model: Listen (understand fully), Acknowledge (validate their concern), Explore (ask probing questions), Respond (address with evidence). Always uncover the real objection behind the stated one. Turn objections into opportunities to demonstrate value. Preparation with objection handling scripts helps.

Negotiation is reaching mutually beneficial agreements. Key principles: (1) Know your BATNA (Best Alternative to Negotiated Agreement), (2) Focus on interests not positions, (3) Aim for win-win outcomes for long-term relationships, (4) Listen more than you talk, (5) Use silence strategically, (6) Justify value before discussing price. Common techniques: anchoring (first offer sets expectations), mirroring, labeling emotions, asking calibrated questions (how/what instead of why).
